chunks.content: Applicability and equipment overview. Manual NX-MCV200-OM-001 version 1.0 applies to the fictional MCV-200 modular conveyor with MC-20 controller, configuration DEMO-A. The assembly includes a conveyor belt, drive motor, guarded drive transmission, entry sensor, operator display and safety interlock circuit. Equipment names such as Conveyor 3 identify individual installations and are not model names. Confirm the model and controller configuration before applying a fault entry; this manual does not cover other conveyor models or controller variants.
chunks.sourceExcerpt: The MCV-200 represents a powered conveyor for moving closed, dry cartons between packaging stations. The fictional assembly includes a conveyor belt, drive motor, guarded drive transmission, entry sensor, operator display and safety interlock circuit. The operator display identifies the active fault code. Equipment names such as "Conveyor 3" identify individual installations. They are not model names. Confirm the model and controller configuration before applying a fault entry; this manual does not cover other conveyor models or controller variants.

chunks.content: Prerequisites before troubleshooting. Confirm the equipment ID, model MCV-200 and controller configuration DEMO-A. Read the complete displayed fault code and record whether the machine is stopped or operating intermittently. Follow the applicable site emergency and hazardous-energy-control procedures. Physical inspection, guard removal, electrical access, blockage removal and repair require appropriately authorized personnel and the prescribed safe condition. A stopped conveyor is not evidence of energy isolation.
chunks.sourceExcerpt: Prerequisite for every fault entry: Follow the applicable site emergency and hazardous-energy-control procedures. Physical inspection, guard removal, electrical access, blockage removal and repair require appropriately authorized personnel and the prescribed safe condition. A stopped conveyor is not evidence of energy isolation.

chunks.content: Observation and maintenance boundaries. An operator may report the display code, time of occurrence, whether movement stopped and conditions noticed before the stop from the normal operator position. Do not reach into the conveyor, touch a motor to assess temperature, remove guards or open an electrical enclosure. Checks of the thermal-protection circuit, drive mechanism, sensor alignment or safety interlocks belong to authorized maintenance personnel. Never bypass an interlock or repeatedly reset a fault. Record actions only when someone confirms they were performed; recommended checks must not be recorded as completed work.
chunks.sourceExcerpt: Checks of the thermal-protection circuit, drive mechanism, sensor alignment or safety interlocks belong to authorized maintenance personnel. The applicable site procedure determines safe access, diagnostic methods and return-to-service authorization. Never bypass an interlock or repeatedly reset a fault to resume production.

chunks.content: Fault-code reference for MCV-200 with MC-20 controller and DEMO-A configuration. E-402 means the controller reports an active motor thermal-protection input; it does not establish that the motor is damaged. E-215 means the entry sensor signal is inconsistent with the expected carton-entry sequence. E-310 means the controller reports an open guard-interlock circuit and inhibits movement. Each code identifies a reported condition, not a verified root cause, and all entries require the prerequisites on page 2.
chunks.sourceExcerpt: The following codes apply only to the fictional MCV-200 / MC-20 DEMO-A configuration. Each code identifies a reported condition, not a verified root cause. All entries require the prerequisites on page 2.

chunks.content: Fault identification limitations. Copy the exact code and accompanying display text, including the sequence of multiple codes when known. Do not choose a code because its description merely resembles a symptom. If a code is not listed, the manual provides no code-specific explanation; record it exactly, capture observed symptoms and refer the issue to maintenance. If no code is displayed, report that fact instead of assigning one. A matching code supports retrieval of guidance but does not prove that a possible cause is present.
chunks.sourceExcerpt: If the code is absent from this table, the manual provides no code-specific explanation. Record the code exactly, capture the observed symptoms and refer the issue to maintenance. If no code is displayed, report that fact instead of assigning one. Similar wording in another fault entry is not sufficient to establish the meaning of an unlisted code. Interpretation boundary: A code match supports retrieval of the relevant guidance. It does not prove that a listed possible cause is present or that a listed corrective action is appropriate.

chunks.content: E-402 documented meaning and possible causes. The controller is receiving an active motor thermal-protection input and inhibits the conveyor drive while that input is active. The indication can be consistent with motor heating, but does not confirm actual motor temperature, permanent damage or the underlying cause. Possible causes requiring investigation include restricted motor cooling, elevated mechanical load, or a fault in the thermal-protection device or signal path. These are possible causes, not confirmed findings.
chunks.sourceExcerpt: E-402 indicates that the controller is receiving an active motor thermal-protection input. In this fictional configuration, the conveyor drive is inhibited while that input is active. The indication can be consistent with motor heating, but the code alone does not confirm the actual motor temperature, permanent motor damage or the underlying cause. 4.2 Possible causes - not confirmed findings Possible cause Information relevant to investigation Restricted motor cooling Obstruction near the cooling path or a change in local ventilation may affect cooling. Elevated mechanical load A change in carton loading or resistance in the drive system may increase motor demand. Thermal-protection signal fault A protection device or its signal path may require investigation even if heating has not been established.

chunks.content: E-402 observations, investigation and escalation. Record when E-402 first appeared, whether the conveyor stopped, whether it recurred, and any noticed change in loading or operating conditions. Record unusual noise or smell only if observed. Do not touch the motor, access guarded areas or restart the conveyor to reproduce the event. After page 2 prerequisites are satisfied, authorized maintenance should assess cooling, mechanical loading and the thermal-protection signal using approved procedures. An unresolved or recurring E-402 requires maintenance review. A report may state: E-402 displayed; conveyor reported stopped; cause not yet confirmed.
chunks.sourceExcerpt: Record the time E-402 first appeared, whether the conveyor stopped, and whether the issue recurred during the shift. Describe any change in loading or operating conditions noticed before the event. Record unusual noise or smell only if actually observed. Do not touch the motor, access guarded areas or restart the conveyor to reproduce the event. 4.4 Recommended maintenance investigation After the page 2 prerequisites are satisfied, authorized maintenance personnel should assess the cooling path, mechanical loading and thermal-protection signal using the applicable approved procedures. These are investigation areas, not a confirmed diagnosis or a prescribed repair sequence. Do not select a replacement motor solely from E-402.

chunks.content: E-215 entry sensor signal inconsistent. The controller cannot reconcile the entry sensor signal with the expected carton-entry sequence; this does not establish that the sensor failed. Possible causes include an obstruction in the sensing area, misalignment, contamination, or a signal-path issue, all requiring maintenance confirmation. Record when the code appeared, whether cartons accumulated and any recent change in carton presentation. Do not reach into the entry area or reposition the sensor. Authorized personnel should investigate the sensing area, alignment and signal under the approved procedure.
chunks.sourceExcerpt: Documented meaning. The controller cannot reconcile the entry sensor signal with the expected carton-entry sequence. The event does not itself establish that the sensor has failed. Possible causes. A carton or other object may be obstructing the sensing area; the sensor may be misaligned or contaminated; or the signal path may require investigation. These alternatives need confirmation by maintenance. Operator observations. Record when E-215 appeared, whether cartons accumulated at the entry and whether there was a recent change in carton presentation. Describe only what can be observed from the normal operator position. Do not reach into the entry area or reposition a sensor to gather evidence. Recommended check and escalation. Authorized personnel should investigate the sensing area, alignment and signal under the approved site procedure. An unresolved or recurring condition requires maintenance review. Record the symptoms; do not state "sensor replaced" or "sensor defective" without evidence.

chunks.content: E-310 guard interlock open. The controller reports an open guard-interlock circuit and inhibits movement. This may represent an open guard or an interlock component or signal-path issue; it does not prove that a switch is defective. Record the code, time, and any guard state visible without approaching a hazard. Do not manipulate guards or operate the machine to test the report. Authorized personnel must investigate under the site-approved safety procedure. Never bridge, bypass or defeat the interlock, and return to service requires the applicable authorization.
chunks.sourceExcerpt: Documented meaning. The controller reports an open guard-interlock circuit and inhibits movement. This may represent an open guard or an issue requiring investigation; it does not prove that a switch is defective. Possible causes. A guard may not be in its intended closed position, or an interlock component or its signal path may require assessment. The code does not identify which of these conditions is present. Operator observations. Record the code, time and any guard state visible without approaching a hazard. Note whether maintenance activity was already in progress if known. Do not manipulate guards or operate the machine merely to test the report. Recommended check and escalation. The responsible authorized personnel should investigate using the site-approved safety procedure. Never bridge, bypass or defeat the interlock. Return to service requires the applicable authorization; acknowledging a report does not provide that authorization.

chunks.content: Minimum breakdown-report information. Record the internal equipment ID, name, model and location without substituting the model for the equipment ID. Record the displayed fault code and the reporting person's symptoms, distinguishing a stopped machine from intermittent operation. Include when the issue was first noticed, recurrence when known, relevant operating changes, and only checks confirmed by the reporting person. Cite manual NX-MCV200-OM-001 version 1.0, the relevant fault page, and prerequisites on page 2. Identify unknown cause and unanswered questions.
chunks.sourceExcerpt: Field What to record Equipment Internal equipment ID, name, model and location. Do not substitute the model for the equipment ID. Observed condition Displayed fault code and the reporting person's symptoms; distinguish a stopped machine from intermittent operation. Timing and context When the issue was first noticed, recurrence if known and relevant changes in operating conditions. Completed checks Only actions confirmed by the reporting person. Leave unknown actions unconfirmed. References Manual NX-MCV200-OM-001, version 1.0; relevant fault page and prerequisites on page 2. Outstanding information Unknown cause, unanswered questions and the responsible maintenance contact or team, if known.

chunks.content: Separate evidence from guidance. Preserve the original report text. A prepared description may organize and clarify observations but must not add an unobserved temperature, failed component, repair, elapsed downtime or completed inspection. Keep possible causes and recommended checks in a separate reference-guidance area. State uncertainty explicitly when a finding has not been established.

A prepared description may organize and clarify those observations, but it must not add an unobserved temperature, failed component, repair, elapsed downtime or completed inspection. Put possible causes and recommended checks in a separate reference-guidance area. State uncertainty explicitly when a finding is not established.

chunks.content: Handover, return to service and document control. Route the report through the site's maintenance process. Return to service requires the applicable authorization; preparing or acknowledging a report does not provide that authorization. Version 1.0 was issued on 12 September 2026. Keep the referenced PDF unchanged and issue a new document version for revised content. The manual contains no spare-parts catalogue, electrical schematics, repair instructions or numeric reset criteria, so missing specifications must not be inferred.
chunks.sourceExcerpt: Route the report using the site's maintenance process. The responsible planner or maintenance team determines assessment, priority and subsequent work planning. Saving or acknowledging a breakdown report does not authorize repair, restart or release of equipment. Immediate hazards follow the site emergency procedure rather than waiting for report completion. 6.4 Routine inspection records Inspection frequency and methods are governed by the approved site maintenance plan; no intervals are prescribed here. Record the date, equipment ID, authorized person, actual observations and follow-up reference. Prior inspection records can provide context but do not establish the cause of a new event. 6.5 Version and scope limits Revision 1.0 is the initial fictional issue dated 12 September 2026. Keep this PDF unchanged when retaining references; issue a new version for revised content. This six-page document contains no spare-part catalogue, electrical schematics, repair instructions or numeric reset criteria. Do not infer missing specifications.
